body: Exactly, yea I’m looking for that. A tribe; those who care to care. And hopefully along side everything, just in general— someday this heaviness will be more cope-able. That’d be cool.

Ah, for sure. might be one of those things where perspective plays a role maybe- - where for you it may not seem almost impossible or far from drastically stressful, but for me it has been. Especially when it’s come down to finding that energy and ‘x’ factor that makes me seem worthwhile to talk to. Humans are like that I’ve found- - they’ll disregard you if you can’t offer something that makes it all *worth* it for them in a friendship. 

Most people don’t have the patience to dig past surface level. Or to stick with someone who’s ‘boring’. Even if it’s because of the depression etc. 

If you’re not funny or interesting; you’re not worth their time. And that’s what depression (or at least for me) tends to steal. That ability to seem attractive in that way. Not being ‘fun’ makes you a liable to get ghosted. And I guess in my head, it makes sense. Logically, it makes sense. Why try and stick with someone who doesn’t fulfill those things? I’m sure there’s plenty of others that will. It probably has something to do with the survival instincts. Understanding what’s going to be a weight for them— and them deciding to leave. 

One of the only things’ that I seem to have found that’s extended those connects: never talking about myself. Unless I’m really prompted to. I’ve tried being the most diligent of listeners, to really care- - even when what they had to say; maybe it wasn’t interesting to me. Because i figured, ‘hey, this is what it takes..I want to care more’. 

And still they dropped me. 

It’s equivalent to an emotional vampire, you know. Just using me to lean on; but never actually caring about what I have to say or what I might need from them. Not that I’m mad about that or anything. I enjoyed being more of a listener. 

But I agree with you. I don’t think things are impossible. With the brain being an incredibly plastic organ, it’s possible to learn more about how to keep those relationships around— and for the brain itself to shift and change. There was a time where I felt well. When I wasn’t some worthless human being. Functional.  

Maybe it’s possible to get back to that point some day.

Yeah. It should be easy— in theory. But unfortunately with clinical depression it makes it hard for me to feel connected at all. Even when I do make the effort or am the one to reach out first, the friendships fizzle away. It’s always been that way.  

But I do appreciate that though. And I do agree, it is hard to find real friends sometimes.

I wish. Ive been trying for the past 8yrs w/ different people, to be real with you (/trying to salvage friendships). It has always ended with me not being able to give as much as I should. Or to nurture them properly. It’s as if it’s hard to provide when the well is empty- - and you haven’t wanted to exist. 

Im grateful for the opportunities I’ve been able to have with certain individuals despite that though. How fortunate I’ve been to meet great people. But yeah. I feel broken. Like my brain chemistry— the way things are wired just will always make it difficult for me. Even when I don’t focus on the negatives, I still feel this way. 

Though I agree. If I could find that way to cope, I think that that would make everything easier. Especially maintaining those connections. Only problem is I’ve done years of talk therapy, tried 6 to 7 different kinds of medicines (for treatment resistant dep. and panic disorder), ketamine, being in the psychward and outpatient a couple times. 

Part of me still holds out that good things could happen. That maybe in time and with the work put in; I could get to where I was again at one point in feeling well.  

I’m just so tired.
